intro.text: A rebellion of the Pahn Kahl against Hallandren, secretly led by Bluefingers, that breaks out while the God King and his queen are shut inside their palace.
A bid by the Pahn Kahl, about three hundred years after the Manywar, to free their people from Hallandren. Led by Bluefingers, it takes over Hallandren's Lifeless army and sends it to march on Idris.

items.text: For centuries the Pahn Kahl have resented Hallandren for conquering them and keeping them in the lowliest work, until most Hallandren assume their culture has vanished.

Before Bluefingers, Vahr led a failed rebellion against Hallandren, raising an army with money from Idrian slumlords and from Hallandren's trade rivals. His capture turned Hallandren's eyes back to Idris, so King Dedelin sent a daughter to marry the God King to put off war.

Bluefingers won Siri's trust after she came to T'Telir, warning her that the priests' push for an heir put her and the God King in danger. She came to ask him to get them out of the palace if they were threatened.

Bluefingers hired Denth's crew to stir up T'Telir. They struck at supplies for the war and, with Vivenna's help, roused the slum-dwelling Idrians. Denth further plotted to kidnap the daughter of Nanrovah, a high priest against war, to blackmail him.

Pahn Kahl disguised as priests seized Blushweaver and tortured her in the tunnels for her Lifeless Command phrases. Lightsong, led there by his dreams, came with Llarimar, and both were caught trying to save her.
Once she gave up her phrase, they killed Blushweaver in front of Lightsong, and got his phrase by threatening Llarimar's life.

With a vote on war coming, the God King's priests shut Siri and Susebron in the palace, claiming she was pregnant. When fighting broke out, Bluefingers offered to lead them out through the tunnels, but Siri saw that this was a Pahn Kahl rebellion led by him, and they made for the front gates instead.

Armed with both phrases, a few Pahn Kahl gave the whole Lifeless army a new Command phrase, and Bluefingers sent it marching on Idris. Everyone who knew the new phrase was to take poison, so no one could call it back.

Bluefingers meant to leave Lightsong's and Blushweaver's bodies in the emptied Lifeless barracks among dead Idrians, so it would look as if they had sent the army to Idris to avenge a murdered God King.

Bluefingers and his Lifeless caught the fleeing party and slew its priests. Susebron went down into the tunnels, and Bluefingers took Siri to a room where he planned to kill her and lay her out among dead Hallandren priests, as if they had brought her to T'Telir to be sacrificed.
In the tunnels Susebron was caged next to Lightsong. When the Pahn Kahl came to kill Susebron, Lightsong spent his divine Breath, giving his own life, to heal the God King's tongue.

Vasher tried to reach Siri but was caught by Denth and his mercenaries. Vivenna freed him, but he had to draw Nightblood and lost most of his Breath, leaving him to face Denth in a duel. Vasher won and killed him.

His tongue healed, Susebron could at last wield the fifty thousand Breaths of Peacegiver's Treasure that he held. Whirling Awakened cloth broke the rebels' hold on the palace, and he freed Siri from Bluefingers.

Vasher and Susebron each thought of chasing the Lifeless army but were talked out of it. Vivenna, learning who Vasher really was, persuaded him to give Susebron the Command phrase for Kalad's Phantoms, and the Phantoms set off after the army marching on Idris.
